items.stem: In the Google Cloud resource hierarchy, which node is the top-level container for an enterprise?

options.rationale: Correct: the Organization is the root node containing folders and projects.
Projects sit beneath folders and the organization.
A VPC is a networking resource, not the hierarchy root.
A billing account pays for usage but is not the hierarchy root.

items.explanation: Correct: the Organization is the root node containing folders and projects.

items.stem: Which TWO are core goals of a Google Cloud landing zone? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Establish a consistent, policy-governed baseline for new workloads
options.rationale: Correct: landing zones provide a governed starting point.

options.text: Separate environments and business units with folders and policies
options.rationale: Correct: structured separation and guardrails are central goals.

options.text: Eliminate the need for IAM entirely
options.rationale: Landing zones rely on IAM, not its removal.

options.text: Force all resources into one project
options.rationale: A flat single project is the opposite of landing-zone design.

items.explanation: Correct: landing zones provide a governed starting point.

items.stem: Why use group-based IAM bindings instead of binding roles to individual users?

options.text: Access management scales and stays consistent as membership changes
options.rationale: Correct: managing access via groups is easier to audit and maintain.
Groups are evaluated by IAM like any principal.
Individual bindings are supported but harder to manage at scale.

options.text: Groups remove the need for least privilege
options.rationale: Least privilege still applies to group roles.

items.explanation: Correct: managing access via groups is easier to audit and maintain.
